claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
A sputter-deposited oxygen-barrier coating will significantly improve the oxidation resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C.
The proposed coating will preserve the alloy's tensile strength at 1000 °C.
The proposed coating will preserve the alloy's tensile ductility.
Sputter deposition will produce a uniform and adherent diffusion-barrier coating on HfNbTaTiZr.
The sputtered coating will form a dense, continuous layer.
The dense, continuous coating will impede oxygen ingress into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Reducing oxygen diffusion will reduce oxidation-scale formation.
Oxidation and oxygen ingress cause embrittlement of HfNbTaTiZr.
Mitigating oxidation-induced embrittlement will maintain the alloy's mechanical properties.
Coated samples will develop a thinner oxidation scale than uncoated samples.
Coated samples will have lower oxygen uptake than uncoated samples.
After exposure, coated samples will retain yield strength and ductility near values measured in inert or lower-temperature environments.
Uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation at 1000 °C.
Oxidation of uncoated HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C reduces ductility and compromises structural integrity.
The coating will remain effective during uninterrupted exposure at 1000 °C for at least 24 hours.
Thermal or mechanical cycling may cause coating degradation or spallation.
Coating degradation or spallation would compromise long-term oxygen-barrier performance.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify tests over 10–24 hours, whereas the boundary states that effectiveness is expected for uninterrupted exposures of at least 24 hours; thus much of the proposed 10–24 hour interval lies outside the stated effective boundary.
